newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks soft in morning, property brings support.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks soft in morning, property brings support.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were soft in Thursday morning trade but grudgingly gave up new record ground as a firm property sector brought support to the market.
The Hang Seng Index was down 37.52 points, or 0.27 percent, at 14,116.06 after briefly rising to an intra-day record of 14,167.01. Turnover was HK$2.80 billion after the first half hour of trade.

Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities, said while the market was suffering from profit-taking after a surge into uncharted ground on Wednesday, Standard & Poor's upgrade of Hong Kong's credit ratings had encouraged foreign investors to invest in Hong Kong.
"There is still some buying in properties," he addded.
Hong Kong's long-term foreign currency rating was raised to A-plus from single-A on Wednesday, while its long-term local currency rating was upgraded to AA-minus from A-plus.
Two companies made their market debuts on Thursday.
Shares of toll road operator Zhejiang Expressway Co Ltd opened for trade at HK$2.75 per share on Thursday compared with an issue price of HK$2.38 each.
Dragonfield Holdings Ltd, a maker of leather garments, also began its first day of trading on Thursday, opening at HK$1.40 compared with an issue price of HK$1.00 each.
